q: Which HTTP method should create a new record?
why: POST creates, GET reads without side effects, PUT/PATCH update, DELETE removes.

q: Why must generated SQL pass user input as ? parameters rather than string-formatting it into the query?
options: DuckDB requires it for SELECT only
why: Parameters keep data separate from the SQL text, so input like '; DROP TABLE' is treated as a value.

q: Which API test is strongest for POST /items?
options: It checks the status code, that the row was stored, and that bad input is rejected
It checks the response time only
why: Cover the happy path and the failure path, and check the effect, not only the status.

q: A request is missing a required field and fails validation in FastAPI/Pydantic. Which status code is returned by default?
why: 422 Unprocessable Entity is FastAPI's default for validation errors. A 500 would mean your code crashed instead.

q: The browser blocks your frontend from calling the API, but curl works. Most likely cause?
options: CORS: the API didn't allow that origin or method
The frontend has too many components
why: CORS is enforced by the browser only. A missing allowed method such as PATCH fails in the browser and passes in curl.

q: Why keep API keys in backend/.env and out of git?
options: Anyone with access to the repo history would get your keys
why: Anything committed is in history forever. Keep secrets in an ignored file and rotate any that leak.

why: A requirement needs a measurable pass condition so a test can prove it. 'Fast' and 'easy' cannot be tested.

q: Why map the API before changing an endpoint?
options: To know what depends on its contract so you do not break it
why: Other code and screens depend on an endpoint's inputs and outputs. Knowing the contract first avoids silent breakage.

q: You wrote a new router and added it to the app, but its endpoints return 404. What is the most likely cause?
options: The backend was not restarted or the router was not registered
why: A router must be included in the app, and a running server needs a restart to load new code.

q: Which states should a data screen handle?
why: Data screens spend much of their life not in the success state. Showing each state clearly avoids blank pages and confusion.
